steps.title: Pale but powerful
steps.body: Nebbiolo gives pale ruby to garnet wines with aromas of rose, violet, red cherry, tar, liquorice and dried herbs, often summed up as tar and roses. It has very high tannin and high acidity, with medium to high alcohol. Its pale colour hides its power, a classic surprise in blind tasting.
steps.highlight: Tar and roses, high tannin and acid

steps.title: Fog and late ripening
steps.body: Nebbiolo's name may come from nebbia, fog, which covers the Langhe hills in autumn when it's harvested, often in October. Or from the white bloom on its berries, like a fog. It's one of the first grapes to bud and the last to ripen, so it needs the warmest, best-exposed slopes. Its skins are low in stable colour pigments, hence the pale colour.

steps.prompt: Why is Nebbiolo pale despite being very tannic?
options: Its skins are low in stable colour pigments
steps.explanation: Nebbiolo has plenty of tannin but few stable pigments, so the colour is light.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for pale ruby with an orange or brick rim, even when quite young. On the nose, rose, cherry, tar and herbs. On the palate, a striking grip of tannin with high acidity. A pale red that grips like Cabernet is almost certainly Nebbiolo.

steps.prompt: Nebbiolo is one of the first grapes to ripen.
steps.explanation: Not true. It buds early but ripens very late, often in October.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Nebbiolo smells of tar and roses, with very high tannin and acidity
Its name may come from nebbia, the autumn fog
